response.content:
## Companies That Entered the German Market in 2026

The German market saw significant new entrants and expansions across multiple sectors in 2026. Here are the notable companies:

### Automotive — Chinese EV Brands Expanding in Germany
- **BYD** climbed to 14th place overall in Germany's passenger car market (October 2026), with 5,173 units sold that month — up 54.3% year on year. BYD continued to broaden its European lineup, launching the budget **Dolphin Surf** (the rebranded Seagull) as its 10th model on sale in Europe.
- **Leapmotor** (via its Stellantis partnership) surged 288.6% in Germany, selling its compact T03 EV at a starting price of €18,900.
- **Geely** entered the German market with the **Monjaro PHEV SUV**, broadening its product range.
- **XPENG** gained ground in Germany; its G6 and G9 SUVs are being assembled at Magna Steyr in Austria for the European market.
- **Lynk & Co** (Geely-owned) took a premium electrification route in Germany, showing sharp year-on-year and month-on-month growth.
- **MG** expanded with the **MG4 Urban**, a compact BEV positioned as a value-for-money city car.

Overall, Chinese brands held 6.4% of the German passenger car market as of October 2026, maturing from price-driven entrants into value-defining contenders.

### Technology & AI
- **Xunce** (Chinese AI data infrastructure company) expanded into Germany with its **TokenOS** product, conducting negotiations with leading European enterprises in automotive, high-end manufacturing, and energy sectors. The company launched a "scenario Token factory" for the European market.
- **Cohere** (Canadian AI startup) merged with Germany's **Aleph Alpha**, combining forces to offer enterprise AI alternatives to Silicon Valley offerings in the European market.

### Banking & Financial Services
- **Crédit Agricole SA** (France) accelerated its expansion in Germany following its acquisition of a business-focused lender, designating Germany as a "priority market."

### Industrial & Manufacturing
- **Hitachi Energy** (Japan/Switzerland) inaugurated its expanded transformer factory in Bad Honnef, Germany in November 2026, with investment exceeding €30 million as part of a global $9 billion manufacturing expansion.

### Workwear & Textiles
- **B2B Wear** (Netherlands) officially entered the German market in September 2026, offering workwear, teamwear, and promotional clothing. Hein Duursma was appointed to lead German operations.

### Defense Sector — New Market Entrants Attracted by Germany's Defense Buildup
Germany's defense spending rose to an estimated €108 billion (2.5% of GDP) in 2026, creating entry opportunities for established defense companies, dual-use technology providers, and specialized suppliers. Germany Trade & Invest identified multiple regional clusters attracting new entrants: Munich/Bavaria (aerospace, land systems), northern Germany (naval, shipbuilding), North Rhine-Westphalia (land systems, munitions), and Berlin (AI, cyber, dual-use innovation).

### Broader Market Context
- Germany set a new six-month startup record in H1 2026, with over 3,053 tech startups founded — an 88% increase year on year. About a third (1,038) were AI-focused.
- German startups raised €8 billion in venture capital between January and September 2026, more than in all of 2025.
- Total business formations reached approximately 525,100 in the first three quarters of 2026, up 7.7% year on year.
- M&A activity involving German companies more than doubled to roughly $26 billion at the start of 2026, with major deals including Deutsche Börse's €5.3 billion acquisition of Allfunds Group and China's Anta Sports acquiring a 29% stake in Puma for €1.5 billion.

Strategic Outlook

Germany's 37% BEV penetration leads Europe, and BEV+PHEV penetration of 48.2% is approaching the halfway mark, yet Chinese brands hold just 6.4% — trust remains thin and pressure persists. BYD's jump into 14th and Leapmotor's 288.6% surge confirm that "PHEV to offset tariffs plus BEV to break in" is one of the current routes into this market. Facing entrenched local barriers, Chinese brands cannot lean on value for money alone; they must evolve from "price challengers" into "long-term choices" through localized R&D, ahead-of-the-curve compliance and long-term service — securing a foothold in the BEV-led first half of electrification and building momentum for the second half of smart technology and local manufacturing.

Germany's BEV+PHEV penetration rose 2.9 percentage points month on month to 48.2%, with Volkswagen ID.7 narrowly edging out Škoda Elroq to lead the BEV segment. Chinese brands are maturing from price-driven entrants into value-defining contenders.

Brand Landscape

Volkswagen (46,331 units, down 4.0% year on year) retained the top spot, followed by Mercedes (26,273 units, up 8.5% year on year) and BMW (23,582 units). BYD (5,173 units, up 54.3% year on year) climbed to 14th overall, while MG, Leapmotor, Geely and XPENG all gained ground — a trend that is accelerating these brands' push into the German automakers' home market.

# Hitachi Energy inaugurates its expanded transformer factory in Bad Honnef, Germany

Press Release | Bad Honnef, Germany | 12.11.2026 | 2 min read

For over 120 years, the site has helped to power Europe’s progress. Today, it builds on the legacy to advance secure, resilient and future-ready grids needed to power the electricity era. [...] > For 120 years, Bad Honnef has been a symbol of German engineering, industrial excellence, and the people whose dedication has powered generations of progress. As we expand for the future of this site, we are not only preserving an important manufacturing heritage, we are also strengthening Germany's industrial base for decades to come. In 2024, we began expanding and modernizing our century old factory with an initial investment of more than 30 million euros. Since then, we have more than doubled our financial commitment to this site: a strong vote of confidence in its people and its future. And with conditions that favour the expansion of transformer manufacturing in Germany, we can do even more. The transformer industry is a strategic enabler of electrification, energy security and [...] Andreas Schierenbeck, CEO of Hitachi Energy

The expansion in Bad Honnef is part of Hitachi Energy’s efforts to increase its global transformer manufacturing footprint as electricity demand grows and power grids are expanded and modernized. Originally announced in February 2024, the expansion includes the construction of the new production hall, installation of new machinery, and the modernization of the existing factory. Globally, Hitachi Energy is investing more than $9 billion in its manufacturing, people and technology, including expanding transformer manufacturing capacity.

context.content: The company's management and representatives participated in relevant events and held in-depth exchanges with stakeholders from all sectors on topics including AI data infrastructure and China-Europe data cooperation. Seizing this opportunity, the company's new-generation product TokenOS is accelerating its entry into the European market, marking a solid step forward in its internationalization strategy. Xunce is conducting in-depth negotiations with multiple leading European enterprises covering core scenarios such as automotive, high-end manufacturing and energy, exploring potential cooperation space for TokenOS and steadily building its global business layout. As a flagship product launched by the company in the first half of this year, TokenOS is dedicated to converting enterprise multi-source heterogeneous data into standardized, measurable and priceable scenario-based Tokens in real time. Prior to this, Xunce has launched a "scenario Token factory" for the European market to promote the localized deployment of TokenOS in Europe. It deeply integrates the engineering capabilities of China's AI data infrastructure with Europe's local industry experience, compliance governance and delivery capabilities, to jointly explore AI transformation solutions that comply with EU data sovereignty requirements.

context.content: # BYD's Budget Dolphin Surf Debuts: Is Europe's EV Market Under Fire? Known for its wallet-friendly EVs, BYD has launched its popular Seagull model in Europe under a new name — the Dolphin Surf. The Seagull has been a runaway success in China, priced around $10,000 and ranking second only to Tesla's Model Y in 2024 with over 442,000 registrations. Global sales of the model are up 45% this year to 170,000 units. Only a few EVs in Europe, such as the Dacia Spring and Leapmotor T03, fall under the €20,000 mark, though several sub-€25,000 models are on the way this year from Renault, Fiat and Hyundai. BYD's Dolphin Surf is the company's 10th model on sale in Europe. **Stellantis** STLA and **Volkswagen** VWAGY are stepping up their EV game as BYD turns up the heat in Europe's affordable EV market. The company has also teamed up with China's Leapmotor to bring the compact T03 EV to Europe at a starting price of €18,900.

More than 3,000 startups were founded in Germany in the ‌first half of 2026, according to economy ministry data. Around a third of the new German companies are AI-focused. # German Business Formation Rises in First Three Quarters of 2026 [...] Larger business start-ups in Germany increased during the first three quarters of 2026, according to the Federal Statistical Office (Destatis). The office reported that roughly 103,700 businesses were founded in the period whose legal form and employee count point to greater economic significance, a rise of 4.5 percent compared with the same period a year earlier.

At the same time, the number of complete closures of businesses of greater economic significance fell 2.4 percent to about 72,500, Destatis said.

## Overall Registrations and Deregistrations [...] ## Overall Registrations and Deregistrations

Total business start-ups reached about 525,100 in the first three quarters of 2026, up 7.7 percent year on year. Total business registrations rose 7.8 percent to about 623,600. Registrations include not only new business formations but also business takeovers such as purchases or the entry of partners, conversions such as mergers or spin-offs, and arrivals from other registration districts.

Complete business closures totaled about 363,500, an increase of 0.8 percent over the prior-year period. Total business deregistrations fell 0.8 percent to about 443,000. Deregistrations also cover business transfers such as sales or partner exits, conversions, and departures to other registration districts.

context.content: Germany's strengths in deep tech and defense have put it in a position to be the fastest-growing ecosystem among Europe's mature VC markets this year. VC funding for German startups reached €6 billion (about $6.8 billion) in the first half of the year, according to PitchBook's **Q2 2026 Germany Market Snapshot**, and is currently pacing for its best year for deal value since 2021's peak. Total investment in Q2 was lower than at the start of the year, but remains in line with the country's quarterly average at €2.1 billion. Should the current funding pace continue, 2026's annual deal value for Germany is expected to be almost 40% above last year's total, a growth rate that surpasses those of its two main competitors, the UK and France. The largest deal to close in the country this year was humanoid startup Neura Robotics' $1.4 billion Series C. Almost half of Europe's most valuable defense tech startups are headquartered in Germany, including Munich-based drone company Helsing, which this month raised a $1.8 billion Series E at an $18 billion valuation.

context.content: Germany's dealmakers are seeing a sharp pickup in activity at the start of 2026, with the value of transactions involving German companies rising to roughly $26 billion since the beginning of the year, according to Bloomberg data. Berlin agreed this week to pay around 3.3 billion for a 25.1% stake in the German unit of power-grid operator Tennet Holding, while Henkel AG (HENOY) said it will acquire Netherlands-based specialty coatings company Stahl Holdings for 2.1 billion. The biggest German deal announced so far this year is Deutsche Boerse's planned 5.3 billion acquisition of European fund distribution platform Allfunds Group, revealed last month, shortly before the Pinault family agreed to sell its 29% stake in Puma to China's Anta Sports Products for 1.5 billion. Bloomberg News has also reported that Blackstone and Yanmar Holdings could be among possible bidders for Volkswagen AG's (VWAGY) Everllence unit, with a deal potentially valuing the business at as much as 6 billion, while Continental AG (CTTAF) is working on a multibillion-euro sale of its ContiTech industrial unit.

context.content:
by Savannah Yawn

Germany’s defense-industrial expansion is creating a new wave of manufacturing investment across the country. German defense expenditures rose from €52.4 billion in 2021 to €107 billion in 2025 and are projected to reach €108 billion, or 2.5% of GDP, in 2026, according to Germany Trade & Invest.

But Germany is not building that capacity from a blank slate.

“Germany combines rising demand with one of Europe’s deepest industrial and innovation bases,” says Christoph Mester, Germany Trade & Invest defense expert. “This creates credible entry opportunities for established defense companies, dual-use technology providers and specialized suppliers seeking to scale in Europe.” [...] Multiple Clusters, One Industrial Shift  
Germany Trade & Invest identifies Munich and Bavaria as a center for aerospace, land systems and defense technology; northern Germany for naval systems, shipbuilding and aerospace; North Rhine-Westphalia for land systems and munitions; and Berlin for artificial intelligence, cyber and dual-use innovation.

“For investors, the result is not one single national cluster, but several specialized ecosystems with distinct market-entry opportunities,” says Mester.

Across Germany, the defense buildout is drawing on industrial capabilities accumulated over generations. Existing factories, skilled manufacturing workers and specialized regional ecosystems are giving companies ways to add capacity quickly as Europe’s security environment changes. [...] One of the clearest examples is in Unterlüß, Lower Saxony, where Rheinmetall invested nearly €500 million in a new ammunition production facility at its existing site. The plant can produce up to 350,000 artillery shells annually once fully ramped.

A second major investment is taking shape in North Hesse. Rheinmetall announced in August 2026 that it will develop a new logistics and technology center at Kassel Airport in Calden. The investment is in the hundreds of millions of euros and includes a logistics center, as well as plans for a drone test center.
